entities.name: Abishua
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abishua (Biblical Hebrew: אֲבִישׁוּעַ) was an early High Priest of Israel, listed in the genealogical tradition as the son of Phinehas and grandson of Eleazar, himself the son of Aaron. He appears in the genealogical lists of 1 Chronicles 6:4–5 and Ezra 7:5 as part of the priestly succession that ran from Aaron through the Zadokite line to the post-exilic priesthood.

As with many figures in the priestly genealogies, Abishua's historical existence is difficult to verify independently, and the lists in which he appears are primarily concerned with establishing legitimate priestly lineage rather than narrating individual biography. His position in the chain — grandson of Eleazar, great-grandson of Aaron — gave him theological significance as part of the unbroken succession legitimising Israelite priestly authority.

The Samaritans venerate Abishua as a significant figure in their own priestly tradition, and the 'Scroll of Abishua' — a document claiming to be the world's oldest Torah scroll, written by Abishua himself — is one of the Samaritan community's most sacred possessions. Most scholars consider the Samaritan scroll a medieval manuscript, but its association with Abishua indicates his importance as a legitimising ancestral figure for Samaritan religious identity.
